subject: Forestry
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: fifty multiple-choice objective questions, all to be answered in 1 hour for 50 marks. Paper 2: six essay-type questions, four to be answered in 2 hours for 20 marks each. Paper 3: practical paper for school candidates (alternative to practical work test for private candidates), four questions all to be answered in 2 hours for 60 marks.
excluded: Preamble, aims and requirements. The syllabus has no country split so all content is included, but much of it is Ghana-specific (named reserves, institutions, permits, land tenure); named reserves and most named agencies were omitted or generalised.

topics.name: Basic Concepts of Forest and Forestry
objectives: Explain the meaning of forest and forestry
Distinguish forestry from agriculture in terms of land occupancy, time frame and risk, and state the business aspects of forestry
State the functions of the forest
Identify the types of plants in the forest (trees, shrubs, herbs, climbers, special plants) and give local and botanical names of timber trees
Describe plant habitats: water-logged (aquatic), dry land, valley/slope, hill tops (terrestrial) and on plants (arboreal), and name the plants found in them
Identify the types of animals found in the forest (birds, insects, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, snails) and the characteristics of their habitats

subtopics.name: Concept of forest ecology
objectives: Describe the characteristics of the forest environment and its physical components
Explain the meaning of forest ecology

subtopics.name: Forest ecosystem
objectives: Explain the meaning of ecosystem and give examples/types of ecosystem in aquatic, terrestrial and arboreal habitats
Describe the major components of the ecosystem and their functions
Explain food chains and food webs and the types of producer-consumer relationships, including symbiotic associations (e.g. rhizobium)
Distinguish saprophytes from epiphytes

subtopics.name: Ecosystem functions
objectives: State the ecosystem functions (regulation, supporting, cultural)
Explain the effects of good and degraded ecosystems on health

subtopics.name: Vegetation zones
objectives: Describe the characteristics of the major vegetation zones and vegetation types in West Africa
Compare the zones in terms of differences in plant species
Describe typical plants and animals, their characteristics and plant and animal associations in the zones
Identify the vegetation types: wet-evergreen, moist-evergreen, moist semi-deciduous, dry semi-deciduous, mangroves and savannah

subtopics.name: Factors affecting distribution of vegetation
objectives: Explain climatic (rainfall and temperature), edaphic (soil) and biotic factors affecting the distribution of vegetation

subtopics.name: Forest types and comparison of forest types
objectives: Describe the distribution, composition and structure of Tropical High Forest (tropical rain forest, tropical moist semi-deciduous forest), savannah, coastal scrub and grassland
Describe the characteristics of virgin or primeval, secondary, natural and artificial forests

subtopics.name: Land use practices in the vegetation zones
objectives: Describe land use practices in the different vegetation zones

subtopics.name: Major forest types in relation to latitudes
objectives: Describe the characteristics of the tropical, temperate coniferous and arctic forest types in relation to latitude
Explain the relationship between temperature and latitude in determining forest types
Describe the characteristics and distribution of angiosperms and gymnosperms

subtopics.name: Concept of wildlife
objectives: Explain the term wildlife and describe wildlife resources

subtopics.name: Identification of wildlife species
objectives: State the common and scientific names of wildlife species

subtopics.name: Importance of wildlife
objectives: State the importance of wildlife to the socio-economy, environment, forestry, tourism and scientific research

subtopics.name: Endangered, rare and common wildlife species
objectives: Give examples of endangered (e.g. elephants), rare (e.g. porcupine) and common (e.g. grasscutter) wildlife species
Explain why the species are in those states

subtopics.name: Wildlife reserves
objectives: Describe the types of wildlife reserves: national parks, game production reserves, wildlife sanctuaries and strict nature reserves, with examples
State the features and location of the various wildlife reserves

subtopics.name: Wildlife management practices
objectives: Describe management practices associated with wildlife reserves and zoos
Describe protection of game reserves against poachers

subtopics.name: Plant parts and functions
objectives: Describe the morphological and anatomical features of plants and their functions
Describe the anatomy of the leaf, stem and roots, including covering tissues such as xylem, phloem, cambium, epidermis, cortex and pith

subtopics.name: Identification of trees
objectives: Identify trees using the observable features of tree parts such as leaves, bark, buttress and stem
State local/trade names and scientific names and apply the rubrics of scientific nomenclature

subtopics.name: Concept of forest estates
objectives: Describe the processes for reservation and constitution of a forest estate
State the role of a Reserve Settlement Commissioner, internal and external pillaring and admitted rights
Distinguish protected forest from non-protected forest

subtopics.name: Management of forest estates
objectives: Describe systems of management and development of public and private estates
Describe forest estate management problems (bushfires, illegal farming, illegal felling, chain-sawing, illegal mining) and their solutions
Explain bushfires as a management problem and as a management tool

subtopics.name: Current state of the forest
objectives: Describe the history of the national forest: area, composition of forest resources and population growth, showing the trend of forest depletion from the past to present, to the current estimate of closed forest

subtopics.name: Protective measures
objectives: Identify forest resources threatened by over-exploitation

Describe measures to stop over-exploitation and protect forest resources: ban on log exports, star rating of species, differential stumpage fees, participatory forestry, yield selection and approval, acquisition of permits and felling rights

subtopics.name: Deforestation
objectives: Explain the term deforestation and its indicators or manifestations in the environment
State the causes of deforestation through human activity: bushfires, farming, felling of trees for various purposes, settlement and urbanization
Explain the effects of deforestation on soil fertility, animal habitat/population, economy and environment

Describe control measures: appropriate farm practices, education, control of indiscriminate tree felling, enforcement of forest laws and regulations, appropriate harvesting and milling equipment, and intervention programmes such as education, rehabilitation, afforestation and reforestation

subtopics.name: Reforestation, afforestation and reafforestation
objectives: Explain the meanings of reforestation, afforestation and reafforestation and the differences between them
Explain silvicultural terminologies: silvics, silviculture, soil seed bank, shade-demanding plants, light-demanding plants, plant succession, forest gaps

subtopics.name: Natural regeneration
objectives: Explain the concept of natural regeneration, soil seed bank and natural gaps
State factors leading to the choice of natural regeneration: topography and slope, type of forest, level and extent of deforestation, occurrence of seed-bearing (mother) trees
Describe the stages of succession (primary, secondary and climatic climax) and give examples of light and shade tolerant trees
State when to use intervention methods such as line and spot planting to supplement natural regeneration, based on the potential of the forest
State the advantages of natural regeneration over artificial regeneration

subtopics.name: Agro-forestry
objectives: Explain the meaning of agro-forestry and carry out practices such as agro-silviculture, alley cropping, mulching and pruning
State characteristics of plants suitable for agro-forestry
State the benefits of agro-forestry: mulch (green manure), pruning material for fodder, companion food, fire wood from the same land, and plant nutrient recycling
Describe silvo-pastoral and agro-silvo-pastoral practices

subtopics.name: Taungya practices
objectives: Explain the concept of taungya and its historical background
State factors/conditions that influence the choice of taungya in a forest estate and its advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.name: Artificial regeneration
objectives: Explain artificial regeneration (forest plantations) with regard to indigenous or exotic species in pure or mixed stands
State the advantages and disadvantages of using exotic species in plantation development

subtopics.name: Invasive alien species
objectives: Identify invasive alien plants, e.g. aquatic: water hyacinth, Kariba weed, water lettuce, Mimosa pigra; terrestrial: Chromolaena odorata, Broussonetia papyrifera, Leucaena leucocephala

subtopics.name: Plantation development
objectives: State the purpose of plantation establishment and the differences between plantation and natural forest

Explain factors influencing plantation development: deficit of wood for industrial and domestic use, level of environmental degradation, need to improve the stocking of existing tree species, need for specific tree type for industrial purposes

subtopics.name: Plantation planning and design
objectives: Plan and design a plantation considering objectives, site selection and preparation, species selection, cost

subtopics.name: Nursery establishment: cultural practices
objectives: State the functions and importance of a nursery as a source of high quality seedlings
Distinguish permanent from flying or temporary nurseries
Carry out bed preparation and cultural practices: pricking out, stumping, stripling, hardening-off, transplanting, seed collection, storage, treatment and sowing, watering, weeding, shading

subtopics.name: Nursery tools and equipment
objectives: Identify nursery tools and equipment such as pick-axe, shovel, rake, hoe, wheel barrow, cutlass, watering can and state their uses

subtopics.name: Nursery pests and diseases
objectives: Identify nursery pests such as slugs/snails and termites, the damage they cause and their control
Identify nursery diseases such as damping off and rust, their symptoms and control

subtopics.name: Costing nursery establishment
objectives: Group nursery costs into direct costs (raw materials, labour, expenses for tools) and indirect costs (stationery and consumables, maintenance, rent of nursery plot)
State ways of controlling nursery cost and of keeping records

subtopics.name: Land preparation
objectives: Clear the site and peg at the required spacing

subtopics.name: Seedling planting
objectives: Use appropriate methods of planting seedlings

subtopics.name: Tending operations
objectives: Carry out tending operations (weeding: complete, spot and line; beating up; pruning; thinning) and state the importance of each
State effects of improper tending: poor height and diameter growth, early branching and poor wood quality

subtopics.name: Operational costs
objectives: Identify sources of operational costs (direct and indirect) and their significance in management
State the kinds of records to be kept on a plantation and the importance of record keeping

subtopics.name: Meaning, importance and purpose of forest mensuration
objectives: Explain forest mensuration and its importance
State its purposes: comparison of current and future states of the forest, determination of quantity of trees, costing and pricing, management

subtopics.name: Measuring instruments and equipment
objectives: Use tools, instruments and equipment for mensuration: Haga altimeter, tape, clinometer, compass, measuring chain, ranging poles and arrows
State the parameters measured and units of measurement in the metric system
Determine height, diameter, girth and volume of trees

subtopics.name: Enumeration of growing stock and sampling methods
objectives: Describe kinds of enumeration (100%, 5%, 2%) of growing stock
Describe sampling methods in forest mensuration (selective, systematic and random sampling)

subtopics.name: Surveys
objectives: Explain survey, kinds of survey (stock survey, strip survey, land survey) and its significance
Use conventional keys/symbols in recording botanical names of trees

subtopics.name: Harvesting of timber: pre-harvesting activities
objectives: State factors to consider before harvesting timber
Describe pre-harvesting activities: stock survey, reconnaissance and field inspections, pre-felling inspection and selection of trees to fell

subtopics.name: Harvesting of timber: procedures
objectives: Describe the procedures for harvesting timber in natural forests and plantations: permit acquisition, yield approval (natural forest), felling, extraction and measurement

subtopics.name: Log markings
objectives: Interpret log markings: property mark, locality mark, compartment number, stock survey number, tree number, reserve code and log number

subtopics.name: Harvesting, extraction and transportation processes
objectives: Describe felling and cross-cutting, hauling, marking, loading and transportation

subtopics.name: Harvesting equipment and safety measures
objectives: Describe harvesting equipment (chain-saw, hand saw, axe, cutlass) with advantages and disadvantages
State safety measures: use of safety gear, directional felling, staff training

subtopics.name: Harvesting of non-timber forest products (NTFPs)
objectives: Give examples of NTFPs: Marantaceae leaves, chewing sticks, plant medicines, canes, rafters, bush meat
Describe methods of harvesting NTFPs: hunting (bushmeat), gathering (leaves, food, snails, medicine, mushroom), trapping (birds, bushmeat), considering safety and sustainability

subtopics.name: Uses of harvested forest products
objectives: State common uses of forest products: shelter, furniture, household utilities, artefacts, food and medicine

subtopics.name: Harvesting of wildlife
objectives: Describe wildlife harvesting techniques (hunting, trapping, baiting, gathering) and their sustainability
Explain endangered, rare and common species and the reasons for those states

subtopics.name: Harmful wildlife harvesting practices
objectives: Describe harmful wildlife harvesting practices such as use of chemicals, fire and gin-trap and measures to control them
State measures to reduce wildlife harvesting: training and education, sanctions and confiscation of harmful equipment, close and open hunting seasons, hunting permits and ban on night hunting

subtopics.name: Classification of forest products
objectives: Classify forest products into direct benefits (timber and non-timber forest products) and indirect benefits (non-tangible products)

subtopics.name: Contribution of forest products to national economy
objectives: Explain the contribution of forest products to income and employment generation

subtopics.name: Demand for forest products
objectives: Describe the role of forest-based industries and the current use of forest products
Explain factors affecting demand: demand spectrum of selected forest products, local and external markets

Identify forest products demanded locally (bushmeat, pestles, wrappers, chewing stick, timber, mushroom, medicinal plants) and by foreign markets (processed timber, medicinal plants, rattan, live animals, animal trophies)
Explain reasons for differences in demand locally and abroad: taste, lifestyle, level of economic development, quality of produce, availability of produce
State socio-economic benefits and effects of demand: increased revenue, employment opportunities and depletion of resources

subtopics.name: Marketing agencies and their functions
objectives: Identify the agencies involved in marketing of forest products (wood products, medicinal plants, wood carving, rattan products) and state their functions

topics.name: Forest Industries and Enterprises in Forestry

subtopics.name: Timber industries and timber products
objectives: Describe different types of forest industries (sawmills, plywood mills, chipboard mills), their locations and sources of raw materials
Explain the contribution of forest industries to the economy: timber processing, range of products, marketing, employment and export earnings
Describe timber processing and its products: sawn boards (2 x 4, 2 x 6, 1 x 8, 1 x 12 etc.), veneer and plywood
Identify sawmilling equipment such as bandmill, slice veneer equipment and rotary veneer equipment

subtopics.name: Career and training opportunities
objectives: Identify forestry training institutions and job opportunities in forestry and forestry-related careers such as carpentry and furniture, wood carving, wood marketing and export

subtopics.name: Establishing enterprises in forestry
objectives: State factors and resources for establishing forest enterprises: identification of business opportunities, identification of a forestry product or service needed; land, capital, materials and structures
Describe procedures for establishing enterprises in forestry

subtopics.name: Policy-making, implementation, monitoring and evaluation
objectives: State the functions of the ministry responsible for forestry and the structures and functions of the Forestry Commission
State the functions of the implementing agencies: Forest Services Division, Wildlife Division and Timber Industry Development Division

subtopics.name: Training and research
objectives: State the roles of forestry training and research institutions in improving the forest industry

subtopics.name: Rights to forest resources
objectives: Describe existing rights governing the use of forest resources: Timber Utilization Contract (TUC), Timber Utilization Permit (TUP), salvage permits for timber and permits for non-timber forest products, and distinguish between them
Describe the procedure for acquiring TUC, TUP and other permits
Identify activities that violate rights (illegal felling, poaching of wildlife, encroachment such as illegal farming and illegal mining)

subtopics.name: Role of stakeholders
objectives: State the roles of stakeholders in sustaining the forest: government sector institutions, traditional authorities and communities, non-governmental organisations and forest-based industries

subtopics.name: Land tenure systems
objectives: Explain the terms and distinguish between alienation rights
Describe the major land tenure systems (communal, individual, leasehold etc.) with their advantages and disadvantages
State the role of stools, skins and central government in land ownership
State the importance and procedure of land registration
Explain the effects of land tenure on land use (e.g. fragmentation, litigation) and ways to improve the land tenure system

subtopics.name: Forest policy and law
objectives: Explain forest and wildlife policy and its importance, e.g. management of forest estate, production of forest industries, manpower training and research, stakeholders' interest
Explain forest and wildlife laws and their importance

subtopics.name: Importance and uses of mushroom
objectives: State the economic, nutritional, medicinal and agricultural uses (of by-products) of mushroom

subtopics.name: Biology of mushroom
objectives: Classify fungi, with emphasis on Basidiomycetes
Distinguish poisonous from non-poisonous mushrooms and commercial from non-commercial mushrooms
Identify mushrooms commonly cultivated in West Africa
Explain how mushroom obtains its nutrients or subsists on substrates/media
Describe the life cycle of mushroom showing the reproduction and production cycles

subtopics.name: Methods of mushroom cultivation
objectives: Describe the steps in the local/pit method, high bed method, low bed method and indoor/commercial/plastic bag method

subtopics.name: Mushroom production practices
objectives: Carry out practices in bag production: composting the substrate, bagging the substrate, sterilizing the bagged compost, inoculation, cropping

subtopics.name: Harvesting and post-harvest handling of mushroom
objectives: Detect signs of maturity and state techniques and precautions in harvesting, frequency of harvest and yield of the different types of mushroom
Process and package mushroom and preserve it by roasting, freezing and canning

subtopics.name: Importance of beekeeping
objectives: State the importance of beekeeping

subtopics.name: Apiary establishment
objectives: Establish an apiary: siting beehives, baiting and capturing

subtopics.name: Members of honey bee colony and their roles
objectives: Describe the characteristics and roles of queens, drones and workers

subtopics.name: Management of an apiary
objectives: Describe routine management practices and precautions to avoid harm to farmers
Control pests and diseases of honey bees

subtopics.name: Maturity of colony, harvesting and processing
objectives: Detect signs of maturity
Describe methods of harvesting and processing of honey, wax and other products

subtopics.name: Marketing of honey and other products
objectives: State strategies for marketing honey and other products

topics.name: Forestry Practical
objectives: Carry out and be assessed on the practical skills in the sub-topics below (Paper 3)

subtopics.name: Practical: introduction to wildlife and plant identification
objectives: Identify and classify wildlife (fauna) using observation skills: footprints, tracks, droppings, size, form, external features and prominent organs
Recognise plant parts (stem form, crown shape, size, texture and arrangement of vegetative parts, colour of flower, fruit) and apply conventional keys
Describe habitats of wildlife and the anatomy of leaves, stems and roots

subtopics.name: Practical: tools, equipment and machinery
objectives: Identify, use and maintain tools, equipment and machinery used in forestry and wildlife management
State the advantages and disadvantages of using the tools

subtopics.name: Practical: nursery practices
objectives: Describe soil treatment methods, seed collection and storage, seed testing and treatment, methods of sowing and planting
Carry out pricking-out, hardening-off and transplanting
Control nursery pests and diseases
Design a calendar for tree nursery development

subtopics.name: Practical: plantation establishment and land preparation
objectives: Design and plan a plantation; survey and clear the site; peg; plant
Carry out thinning, pruning, weeding, beating up and record keeping

subtopics.name: Practical: forest mensuration
objectives: Determine height, diameter, girth and volume of trees and NTFPs and angles of slopes
Use units of measurement and conventional symbols

subtopics.name: Practical: methods of harvesting timber
objectives: Describe felling operations, safety measures and procedure for harvesting
Interpret log markings (property mark, locality marks, compartment number, stock survey number, tree number, reserve code, log number)

subtopics.name: Practical: methods of harvesting non-timber forest products
objectives: Describe existing harvesting practices: hunting wildlife (bushmeat), collection (snails, mushroom), gathering (leaves, food, medicine), trapping (wildlife)
Describe harmful harvesting practices

subtopics.name: Practical: processing of timber
objectives: Identify types of processed forest products, e.g. veneer, plywood, particle board, artefacts (wood carvings)
Describe methods of processing timber into these products

subtopics.name: Practical: processing of non-timber forest products
objectives: Identify rattan, bamboo, mushrooms, snails, bush meat, medicinal plants etc. and state their processing and preservation methods and uses

subtopics.name: Practical: mushroom cultivation
objectives: Identify kinds of mushroom
State uses, methods of cultivation, production, harvesting, processing and preservation practices

subtopics.name: Practical: beekeeping
objectives: Identify members of the bee colony and state their roles and the uses of bee products
Describe management, harvesting, processing and marketing activities
